svg.aria-label: state is one number per (key, window) pair
svg.text: State as a fold — rebuildable from the stream, and only that way
7 entries · rebuild reads 9 events, resume reads 4 · 1 never collectable
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = which group it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the keys state is held per. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: CHK — the index the checkpoint in this chapter was taken at. CHK = 4
13 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
15 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
16 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest event time through i, minus LAG.
22 // primitive: entryOf(e) — the (key, window) pair this event belongs to. That pair
23 // is the UNIT of streaming state; there is one number per pair.
26 // function: buildFrom(startIndex, prior) — fold the stream from startIndex into
27 // `prior`, counting the events read. prior = NONE means "rebuild from scratch".
41 // primitive: windowOf(entryId) — the window start inside an entry id.
44 // function: collectableAt(entryId) — the index at which the watermark passes that
45 // entry's window end, so its memory may be released. NONE means never.
54 // function: permanent(st) — entries nothing will ever collect. Persistence makes
55 // these survive restarts instead of being cleared by one.
65 // function: main() — THE CALLER: rebuild from scratch, and resume from CHK.
68 val loaded = buildFrom(0, NONE) // stands for the checkpointed prefix
Step 1/0 — state is one number per (key, window) pair
`id` is `"a@480"` — a key and a window start, nothing else. 9 events produce 7 such ids, so "state" is 7 numbers. Everything in this chapter exists to carry
